~/uet-dbms$ dc exec pg pg_test_fsync -s 5 -f /var/lib/postgresql/data/fsync_test.tmp | tee results/env/pg_test_fsync.txt
5 seconds per test
O_DIRECT supported on this platform for open_datasync and open_sync.

Compare file sync methods using one 8kB write:
(in wal_sync_method preference order, except fdatasync is Linux's default)
        open_datasync                       417.042 ops/sec    2398 usecs/op
        fdatasync                           423.879 ops/sec    2359 usecs/op
        fsync                               210.448 ops/sec    4752 usecs/op
        fsync_writethrough                              n/a
        open_sync                           211.247 ops/sec    4734 usecs/op

Compare file sync methods using two 8kB writes:
(in wal_sync_method preference order, except fdatasync is Linux's default)
        open_datasync                       211.988 ops/sec    4717 usecs/op
        fdatasync                           419.513 ops/sec    2384 usecs/op
        fsync                               210.346 ops/sec    4754 usecs/op
        fsync_writethrough                              n/a
        open_sync                           105.020 ops/sec    9522 usecs/op

Compare open_sync with different write sizes:
(This is designed to compare the cost of writing 16kB in different write
open_sync sizes.)
         1 * 16kB open_sync write           210.177 ops/sec    4758 usecs/op
         2 *  8kB open_sync writes          104.772 ops/sec    9545 usecs/op
         4 *  4kB open_sync writes           52.686 ops/sec   18980 usecs/op
         8 *  2kB open_sync writes           26.408 ops/sec   37867 usecs/op
        16 *  1kB open_sync writes           13.112 ops/sec   76265 usecs/op

Test if fsync on non-write file descriptor is honored:
(If the times are similar, fsync() can sync data written on a different
descriptor.)
        write, fsync, close                 210.057 ops/sec    4761 usecs/op
        write, close, fsync                 209.603 ops/sec    4771 usecs/op
